pages.headline: SC splits on Section 17A of PC Act
pages.what: A two-judge bench of Justices B.V. Nagarathna and K.V. Viswanathan delivered a split verdict on Section 17A, which needs prior approval before a public servant's official decisions are investigated. The matter now goes to CJI Surya Kant for a larger bench.
key: Section 17A was inserted by the 2018 amendment to the PC Act, 1988
Nagarathna J struck it down: violates Article 14; Section 19 already protects officials
Viswanathan J upheld it, but approval must come from an independent authority (Lokpal/Lokayuktas)
Split verdict, so a larger bench will be constituted by the CJI
pages.static: Article 14 (equality); Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988; Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
pages.angle: Swapping which judge struck down and which upheld the provision.
pages.remember: Nagarathna Negates, Viswanathan Validates (with conditions).

pages.headline: States told to frame police briefing policy
pages.what: The Supreme Court directed every State to frame a policy on police media briefings within three months. It should follow a manual prepared by amicus curiae Gopal Sankaranarayanan. The proceedings arose from PUCL petitions. Briefings aim to prevent harm, correct rumours and release only verified information.
key: Deadline: three months for all States
Model: manual by amicus curiae Gopal Sankaranarayanan
Arose from PUCL petitions
PUCL v. State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down 16 guidelines on police encounters
Purpose: prevent harm, correct rumours, release verified facts
pages.static: Article 21 (fair trial and reputation); police is a State subject (List II, Entry 2).
pages.angle: Attributing the 16 encounter guidelines to a different police-reform case.
pages.remember: PUCL 2014: sixteen encounter guidelines; 2026: briefing policy in three months.

pages.headline: Is the ED a juristic person? SC to examine
pages.what: The Supreme Court agreed to hear petitions by Tamil Nadu and Kerala asking whether the Enforcement Directorate is a juristic person that can approach High Courts under Article 226. The States say a statutory body has only expressly granted powers, and the ED has no power to sue.
key: Question: is ED a juristic person entitled to move High Courts (Art 226)?
Petitioners: Tamil Nadu and Kerala
States' argument: statutory bodies hold only expressly granted powers
Kerala: State inquiry commission in a gold smuggling matter
Tamil Nadu: illegal mining case
pages.static: Article 226 (High Court writ jurisdiction); FEMA, 1999; PMLA, 2002.
pages.angle: Reversing the States' argument about the ED's power to sue.
pages.remember: States say ED may not sue: no express power in FEMA or PMLA.

pages.headline: SC seeks Centre's reply on Arbitration Council
pages.what: The Supreme Court asked the Union government to respond to a petition seeking constitution of the Arbitration Council of India. The statutory body was created on paper by the 2019 amendment but has not been set up nearly six years later.
key: Statutory body under Part IA, Sections 43A to 43M, of the 1996 Act
Inserted by the Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Act, 2019
Based on the Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee (2017)
Still not constituted nearly six years on
pages.static: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996; Article 39A and access to justice.
pages.angle: Assuming a body created by statute has actually been set up.
pages.remember: Law made in 2019, Council still missing.

pages.headline: SC on POCSO and teenage relationships
pages.what: In State of Uttar Pradesh v. Anurudh (2026), the Supreme Court noted the increasing use of POCSO against consensual adolescent relationships and urged the Union government to consider corrective measures. The debate on a 'Romeo-Juliet' clause is linked.
key: Case: State of Uttar Pradesh v. Anurudh (2026)
Age of consent: 18 under POCSO and BNS Section 63
Section 19 POCSO: mandatory reporting
Age of Consent Act, 1891 raised age from 10 to 12
pages.static: POCSO Act, 2012; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023; Age of Consent Act, 1891.
pages.angle: Believing the age of consent is 16.
pages.remember: Eighteen everywhere: POCSO and BNS 63.

pages.headline: Allahabad HC: DMF is beneficial legislation
pages.what: The Allahabad High Court held that the creation of District Mineral Foundations is beneficial legislation, to be interpreted liberally in favour of those adversely affected by mining. DMFs are trusts funded by royalty contributions from mining lessees.
key: DMF: statutory non-profit trust, Section 9B, MMDR Act, 1957 (inserted 2015)
Contribution: 30% of royalty for leases before 12 Jan 2015
Contribution: 10% of royalty for later leases
Spent under PM Khanij Kshetra Kalyan Yojana
At least 60% for high-priority areas
pages.static: MMDR Act, 1957; Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas; PMKKKY.
pages.angle: Swapping the 30% and 10% royalty shares.
pages.remember: Old leases pay thirty, new leases pay ten.

pages.headline: UGC notifies 2026 equity regulations
pages.what: The University Grants Commission notified the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026. They replaced the 2012 rules, which had been framed after the Abeda Salim Tadvi case, and set strict deadlines for handling complaints of discrimination.
key: Replace the 2012 equity framework
Every HEI: Equal Opportunity Centre plus Equity Committee
Committee meets within 24 hours; reports in 15 days
Head of institution acts within 7 days
Equity Squads, 24x7 helpline, Equity Ambassadors; penalty up to loss of recognition
pages.static: UGC Act, 1956; Articles 14, 15 and 17; Abeda Salim Tadvi v. Union of India (2019).
pages.angle: Mixing up the 15-day report deadline and the 7-day action deadline.
pages.remember: Meet in one day, report in fifteen, act in seven.

pages.headline: SC stays UGC equity rules
pages.what: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi stayed the 2026 UGC equity regulations, calling them prima facie vague and capable of misuse. The 2012 Regulations continue until further orders, and notice was issued on three petitions alleging discrimination against the general category.
key: Bench: CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi
Reason: prima facie vague, capable of misuse
2012 Regulations continue (Article 142 used)
Notice to Union and UGC; returnable on 19 March
Court suggested a committee of eminent jurists revisit the rules
pages.static: Article 142 (complete justice); Article 14 and affirmative action in education.
pages.angle: Thinking a stay creates a vacuum rather than reviving the earlier rules.
pages.remember: Stay on 2026; 2012 lives on.

pages.headline: Menstrual hygiene is part of Article 21
pages.what: The Supreme Court, hearing a petition by Dr. Jaya Thakur, held that menstrual health and hygiene management in schools are part of the right to life and dignity under Article 21. It directed States and UTs to provide facilities in every school.
key: Right: Article 21 (life and dignity)
Petitioner: Dr. Jaya Thakur
Functional gender-segregated toilets in schools
Free sanitary napkins through vending machines
Menstrual hygiene management corners
pages.static: Article 21; Article 21A; Article 47 (public health).
pages.angle: Calling the right a mere Directive Principle.
pages.remember: Dignity at school: Article 21, not just a policy wish.

pages.headline: Governors' addresses in Tamil Nadu and Kerala
pages.what: Tamil Nadu's Governor walked out of the Assembly during the customary address, and Kerala's Governor omitted paragraphs of his address. The episodes revived debate on Article 176, which requires the Governor to address the legislature at the start of the first session each year.
key: Article 176: mandatory address, first session each year and after general elections
Article 175: Governor may address; not mandatory
Speech is drafted by the Council of Ministers
Precedents: Shamsher Singh (1974), Nabam Rebia (2016)
Sarkaria (1988) and Punchhi (2007) Commissions
pages.static: Articles 159, 175, 176; Governor as constitutional head.
pages.angle: Confusing optional Article 175 with mandatory Article 176.
pages.remember: Article 176 is a must; 175 is a may.

pages.headline: Governor's Rule extended in Chakma ADC
pages.what: The Mizoram Governor extended Governor's Rule in the Chakma Autonomous District Council by six months, despite opposition from the State Cabinet. The rule was first imposed in July 2025. The council was constituted in 1972 under the Sixth Schedule.
key: Extension: six months, over State Cabinet's objection
First imposed in July 2025
Chakma ADC created 1972 under the Sixth Schedule
ADC: up to 30 members (26 elected, up to 4 nominated), five-year term
Bodoland Territorial Council has 46 members
pages.static: Sixth Schedule (Articles 244(2), 275(1)); Governor's role in tribal areas.
pages.angle: Taking the Cabinet to have backed the extension.
pages.remember: Sixth Schedule: 26 elected plus 4 nominated.

pages.headline: Kerala passes Malayalam Language Bill, 2025
pages.what: The Kerala Assembly passed a Bill to give Malayalam primacy in administration, schools and courts. It removes or modifies the provisions that sank the State's 2015 language Bill, which the President had refused assent after reservation.
key: Malayalam compulsory first language in government and aided schools
Bills and Ordinances to be introduced in Malayalam; judgments translated in phases
Official Language department to be renamed Malayalam Language Development Department
2015 Bill reserved for the President; assent withheld
Objections then: Official Languages Act 1963, minorities, three-language formula, RTE Act
pages.static: Article 345 (State official language), Articles 200-201 (reservation of Bills for the President).
pages.angle: Assuming the 2015 Bill was cleared; it was reserved and assent was withheld.
pages.remember: 2015 Bill stalled at the President; 2025 Bill redrafted.

pages.headline: Himachal Pradesh marks 56th Statehood Day
pages.what: Himachal Pradesh celebrated its 56th Statehood Day on 25 January 2026. It became the 18th State on 25 January 1971 under the State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970, after passing through several lower constitutional statuses.
key: Chief Commissioner's Province: 15 April 1948
Part C State: 1950
Union Territory: 1 November 1956
18th State: 25 January 1971
Law: State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970
pages.static: Article 3 and 4; States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (abolished Part C).
pages.angle: Placing UT status before Part C status.
pages.remember: Commissioner, Part C, UT, State: 1948 to 1971.

pages.headline: 28th CSPOC inaugurated in New Delhi
pages.what: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 28th Conference of Speakers and Presiding Officers of the Commonwealth in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla was in the chair, and 61 presiding officers from 42 Commonwealth countries and 4 semi-autonomous parliaments attended.
key: Date: 15 January 2026, Samvidhan Sadan Central Hall
Delegates: 61 presiding officers from 42 countries and 4 semi-autonomous parliaments
India hosted earlier in 1971, 1986 and 2010
CSPOC created 1969 on Canadian Speaker Lucien Lamoureux's initiative; Canada gives secretariat
Commonwealth has 56 members
pages.static: Role of the Speaker (Articles 93-96); Commonwealth Parliamentary Association.
pages.angle: Crediting India with founding CSPOC or hosting its secretariat.
pages.remember: Founded by Canada in 1969; India hosts every few decades.

pages.headline: Budget Session 2026 begins
pages.what: The Budget Session of Parliament began on 28 January 2026 and ran until 18 April 2026. Nine Government Bills were passed, including the Finance Bill, 2026 and two Appropriation Bills.
key: Began 28 January 2026; ended 18 April 2026
Nine Government Bills passed
Finance Bill, 2026 and two Appropriation Bills among them
Also passed: Transgender Persons Amendment Bill 2026
Also: CAPF (General Administration) Bill, Jan Vishwas Bill, Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Bill
pages.static: Articles 112-117 (budget, Appropriation and Finance Bills).
pages.angle: Forgetting that Appropriation Bills are passed alongside the Finance Bill.
pages.remember: Budget session: Finance Bill plus two Appropriation Bills.

pages.headline: ECI hosts IICDEM 2026; ECINET launched
pages.what: The Election Commission hosted the first India International Conference on Democracy and Election Management at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. ECINET was launched during it and the Delhi Declaration 2026 was adopted. Nearly 100 delegates from over 70 countries were expected.
key: First IICDEM, Bharat Mandapam, from 21 January 2026
Organiser: IIIDEM (set up 2011, Dwarka)
ECINET integrates over 40 ECI apps in one platform
Delhi Declaration 2026 adopted
Nearly 100 delegates from over 70 countries expected
pages.static: Article 324 (Election Commission); Representation of the People Acts.
pages.angle: Mistaking ECINET for a voting technology instead of an integrated app platform.
pages.remember: ECINET: forty apps, one platform.

pages.headline: Delimitation and Southern States' concerns
pages.what: Southern States said population-based delimitation of Lok Sabha seats and Finance Commission transfers penalise States that controlled population growth. The debate revived the rules and history of delimitation.
key: Articles 82 and 170: readjustment; Articles 330 and 332: SC/ST seats
Commissions constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002
J&K 2022: 90 Assembly seats (43 Jammu, 47 Kashmir), 5 Lok Sabha seats
Orders have force of law; cannot be modified by Parliament or Assemblies
SC (2024) can review manifestly arbitrary orders
pages.static: Articles 81, 82, 170, 330, 332; Delimitation Commission Act, 2002.
pages.angle: Believing Parliament can amend a Commission's order.
pages.remember: Commission order = law; no House can edit it.

pages.headline: Nitin Nabin elected BJP national president
pages.what: Nitin Nabin, the BJP's working president and a Bihar minister representing Bankipur, was elected national president on 20 January 2026. He became the party's youngest national president. The result was announced by national returning officer Dr K. Laxman.
key: Elected 20 January 2026
Youngest national president of BJP
Earlier working president; Bihar minister from Bankipur
Earlier headed BJYM in Bihar
Returning officer: Dr K. Laxman
pages.static: Political parties and party organisation (Tenth Schedule context).
pages.angle: Mixing him up with a Chief Minister or a general secretary.
pages.remember: Nabin: youngest BJP chief.

pages.headline: Praveen Vashista appointed Vigilance Commissioner
pages.what: The President appointed Shri Praveen Vashista as Vigilance Commissioner in the Central Vigilance Commission under Section 4(1) of the CVC Act, 2003. The CVC was set up in 1964 and became statutory in 2003.
key: Appointed under Section 4(1) of the CVC Act, 2003
CVC set up 1964 on Santhanam Committee recommendation
Statutory status: CVC Act, 2003
Selection committee: PM, Union Home Minister, Leader of Opposition (Lok Sabha)
Tenure: four years or age 65
pages.static: CVC Act, 2003; Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962-64).
pages.angle: Assuming CVC has been statutory since its 1964 start.
pages.remember: Santhanam 1964, statute 2003.

pages.headline: Lokpal marks Foundation Day
pages.what: The Lokpal of India observed its Foundation Day on 16 January, marking the day Section 3 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 came into force in 2014. The Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to eight members.
key: 16 January 2014: Section 3 of the 2013 Act in force
Chairperson plus up to eight members
At least 50% judicial members
Selection Committee: PM, Speaker, Leader of Opposition, CJI or nominee, eminent jurist
First Lokayukta: Maharashtra, 1971
pages.static: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013; Administrative Reforms Commission (1966).
pages.angle: Saying all members must be judicial.
pages.remember: Half judicial, at least.

pages.headline: NDSA show-cause notice over Bargi Dam
pages.what: The National Dam Safety Authority issued a show-cause notice to the Narmada Valley Development Authority over safety concerns at the Bargi Dam on the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh. The NDSA is a statutory body under the Dam Safety Act, 2021.
key: Dam: Bargi Dam, Narmada River, Madhya Pradesh
Notice to Narmada Valley Development Authority
NDSA: statutory body under Dam Safety Act, 2021
NDSA headquarters: New Delhi
Bargi built 1974 to 1990 as a multipurpose dam
pages.static: Dam Safety Act, 2021; water is a State subject (Entry 17, List II).
pages.angle: Placing Bargi on the wrong river or wrong State.
pages.remember: Bargi on Narmada, NDSA on notice.

pages.headline: Indore water contamination exposes urban water governance
pages.what: Contaminated municipal tap water in Indore caused infections and multi-organ failure among residents. The NHRC took suo motu cognizance after finding the supply main ran under a public toilet.
key: NHRC suo motu cognizance; pipeline beneath a public toilet
Water supply: State subject; 74th Amendment widened municipal role
BIS standard: IS 10500 (drinking water)
AMRUT 2.0 (MoHUA) includes Pey Jal Survekshan
Non-revenue water about 38% of supply
pages.static: Twelfth Schedule; AMRUT 2.0; Jal Jeevan Mission (Urban).
pages.angle: Crediting AMRUT to the Jal Shakti Ministry.
pages.remember: AMRUT = housing and urban ministry; IS 10500 = BIS.

pages.headline: 50th PRAGATI meeting held
pages.what: The Prime Minister held the 50th PRAGATI review. The platform brings Union and State officials together to resolve stalled projects, and has unlocked long-pending ones.
key: PRAGATI = Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation; launched 2015
Chaired by the Prime Minister
Hosts PM Gati Shakti, PARIVESH, PM Reference Portal
About 94% of issues resolved
Examples: Jammu-Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla rail link, Navi Mumbai airport, Bogibeel bridge
pages.static: Cooperative federalism; PM Gati Shakti; PARIVESH single-window clearance.
pages.angle: Naming the Cabinet Secretary or NITI Aayog as chair.
pages.remember: PRAGATI: PM in the chair, since 2015.

pages.headline: Land Stack and Glossary of Revenue Terms launched
pages.what: The Ministry of Rural Development launched Land Stack, a GIS-based integrated digital platform for land records, in pilot locations Chandigarh and Tamil Nadu. It also released a Glossary of Revenue Terms to harmonise land-revenue vocabulary.
key: Land Stack: GIS-based integrated platform for land records
Pilot sites: Chandigarh and Tamil Nadu
Runs under DILRMP
Inspired by models in Singapore, the UK and Finland
Glossary of Revenue Terms in vernacular, Hindi, English and Roman scripts
pages.static: Land is a State subject (Entry 18, List II); DILRMP.
pages.angle: Attributing the launch to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
pages.remember: Land Stack: Rural Development, GIS, DILRMP.

pages.headline: Census 2027 notified
pages.what: The Ministry of Home Affairs notified the 16th Census. Phase I, house-listing, runs from 1 April to 30 September 2026, with a 30-day window per State or UT and a 15-day self-enumeration option beforehand. Phase II has a reference date of 1 March 2027. It is India's first digital census.
key: Phase I: 1 April to 30 September 2026
30-day window per State/UT; 15-day self-enumeration first
Phase II reference date: 1 March 2027
Snow-bound areas: 1 October 2026
First digital census and first nationwide caste count since 1931
pages.static: Census Act, 1948; Union List Entry 69.
pages.angle: Mixing the snow-bound reference date with the general one.
pages.remember: One March 2027; snow-bound areas one October 2026.
